newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude slides with NYMEX, rumored sales.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude slides with NYMEX, rumored sales.

text.p: U.S. West Coast oil prices plunged Friday, pressured by sharply lower futures values and rumors the local benchmark grade was selling at heavy discounts in other regions, traders said.

Although no sales of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were reported, buyers claimed the grade's largest seller sold a waterborne cargo to U.S Gulf refiner for $2.00 under July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on Thursday.
The $2.00 discount excluded the cost of transporting the barrels.
The seller declined comment on the sale.
Another rumor was ANS was delivered to Midland in the Midcontinent for $2.50 under WTI. That was the equivalent of a minus $3.50 -$4.00 sale on the West Coast, buyers said.
Meanwhile, crude oil futures for July delivery slid 87 cents a barrel, amid technical selling.
In local trade, at least two typical buyers of ANS wanted to sell in July as increased South American grades and poor refinery profits left them with unwanted ANS.
That left five sellers, more than the number of prospective buyers.
Buyers expect the next ANS cargo to sell wider than $2.25 a barrel off July WTI.
ANS outright prices eased 80 cents a barrel on the day in line with weaker futures and cash WTI markets.
Overall, traders are concerned about a supply glut, following a report by the American Petroleum Petroleum Tuesday that crude inventories rose a sharp 8.4 million barrels nationwide last week.
